bank.question: Which three methods are the most effective for a supervisor to ensure a team understands the site-specific hazards?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A, C and D. Site inductions, Daily Activity Briefings (DABs), and toolbox talks are primary ways supervisors ensure workers understand specific site risks
options: Toolbox talks before specific tasks begin
Annual corporate newsletters sent to head office
Daily Activity Briefings (DABs) at the start of the shift
Mandatory site inductions for all new arrivals

bank.question: Who is responsible for the cost of providing mandatory Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) to employees?
bank.explanation: Health and safety law generally places the duty on the employer to provide necessary PPE at no cost to the employee
options: The employer
The employee
The Health and Safety Executive (HSE)
The client's insurance company

bank.question: A 'Permit to Work' system is a formal written system used to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous
bank.explanation: This is true because while not always a legal requirement for all small firms, a permit-to-work system is a standard industry 'best practice' for managing high-risk activities like confined spaces

bank.question: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act, which two responsibilities apply specifically to employees (operatives)?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A and D. The Health and Safety at Work Act (Section 7) requires employees to look after themselves and others, and to cooperate with their employer on safety matters

To write their own Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS)
To pay for their own basic Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
To cooperate with their employer on health and safety matters

bank.question: What is the primary purpose of delivering a 'Toolbox Talk' to a work crew?
bank.explanation: Toolbox talks are short, focused briefings on specific risks or procedures relevant to the current site tasks
options: To provide a formal 3-year health and safety certificate
To discipline workers for minor safety breaches
To deliver specific, short-duration safety briefings on relevant site hazards
To replace the need for an initial site induction

bank.question: Which two actions should a supervisor take to ensure electrical safety on site?

Using high-voltage (230v) tools without a transformer to increase speed
Confirming that 110v (yellow) power is used for hand tools and site lighting
Running electrical cables across busy site haul roads without protection

bank.question: Under the CDM Regulations 2015, when is a project considered 'notifiable' based on duration and the number of workers?

20 Working days and 15 workers
30 Working days and more than 20 workers
50 Working days and 5 workers

bank.question: Who has a legal duty under the Health and Safety at Work Act to take care of the health and safety of themselves and others?

Only the Client and the Site Manager
Only the Supervisor and the Safety Officer
Everyone on the site, including workers and supervisors

bank.question: A competent person has the right combination of skills, knowledge, experience and training for the task

bank.question: When issuing tight-fitting respirators (RPE) to workers, which three factors must a supervisor ensure?

The worker is clean-shaven to ensure an effective facial seal
The mask is compatible with other PPE being worn (e.g. eye protection)
The worker has owned the mask for more than twelve months

bank.question: A team is starting work near a high-risk activity being carried out by another contractor. What should the supervisor do first?

Allow them to work provided they wear high-visibility clothing
Brief them on the specific risks and exclusion zones of the other work
Wait for the other work to finish before starting any new tasks

bank.question: When overseeing tasks that generate wood dust, which three controls should be implemented according to the hierarchy of control?

Ensure an 'on-tool' dust extraction (LEV) system is used
Rely solely on standard surgical masks for protection
Plan the work to minimise the amount of cutting required

bank.question: Which document should be used to record how waste materials are managed and disposed of on a construction project?

options: Site Waste Management Plan (SWMP)
COSHH Register
Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA)
Method Statement

bank.question: Workers may ignore RAMS once they have several years of experience
bank.explanation: This is false because RAMS set the agreed controls for the task and must be followed regardless of experience.

bank.question: What is considered the most effective way to manage waste on a construction site according to the waste hierarchy?

Reducing the amount of waste produced (prevention)
Finding a cheaper waste removal contractor
Sending all rubble to a designated landfill site

Carrying out professional medical diagnoses for workers who feel unwell
Ensuring adequate ventilation and extraction in confined work spaces
Conducting regular blood tests to check for occupational diseases

bank.question: Under the Temporary Works procedures, when must a supervisor ensure an inspection takes place? (Select two)

Only once every six months, regardless of usage or weather
Immediately after a worker has finished their lunch break
Before the temporary work is used for the first time each day/shift

bank.question: Site-specific inductions are a legal requirement for all workers before they start work on a new construction site

bank.question: When cutting paving slabs or bricks with a power saw, what is the most significant respiratory health hazard?

Carbon monoxide gas
Nitrogen dioxide fumes
General household dust

bank.question: What is a key responsibility of a supervisor regarding Safe Systems of Work (SSoW)?

options: Doing the most dangerous tasks themselves to protect the team
Focusing only on meeting the project deadlines regardless of safety
Completing all the physical work to ensure it is done correctly
Ensuring that workers follow the agreed safe systems of work (SSoW)

bank.question: What is the main reason for encouraging workers to report 'near-miss' incidents?
bank.explanation: Near-miss reporting is vital for identifying trends and implementing controls before a real injury occurs

To find out which worker is to blame for the error
To increase the insurance premiums for the subcontractor
To fill out the site diary when there is no other progress to report

bank.question: What is the primary danger associated with working in a 'confined space'?

The lack of adequate lighting for the job
The potential for a toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere
The difficulty of using mobile phones for communication

bank.question: Which two items should be checked when reviewing welfare arrangements on a site?

Drinking water and rest facilities are adequate
Workers bring all welfare supplies from home
Welfare is only provided after the project reaches second fix

bank.question: Which three actions should a supervisor take before allowing work to start in a newly excavated area?

Confirm access and edge protection are suitable
Assume the excavation is safe if it was dug the same day
Ensure spoil and materials are kept away from the edge

bank.question: Managers should consider both safety hazards and health risks when planning construction work
bank.explanation: This is true because construction planning must address immediate injury risks and long-term exposures.

bank.question: When overseeing a complex lifting operation using a crane, which three statements are correct?

The lift plan is only required if the lift exceeds 10 tonnes
All personnel involved must be briefed on the plan before the lift starts
The plan must include the weight of the load and the lifting accessories

bank.question: According to the Work at Height hierarchy, which three conditions must be met to justify using a ladder?

If the task is low-risk and of short duration (less than 30 mins)
If three points of contact can be maintained while climbing
If a more suitable work platform (like a podium) cannot fit in the area

bank.question: Which three responsibilities belong specifically to the Principal Contractor under CDM 2015?

Providing site inductions for all workers and visitors
Paying the wages of all subcontractor employees
Providing and maintaining welfare facilities

bank.question: Which two statements accurately reflect a supervisor's duties regarding COSHH (Control of Substances Hazardous to Health)?

The assessment must be specific to how the product is used on this site
Assessments only need to be reviewed if a serious injury occurs
Workers must be informed of the risks and control measures identified in the assessment

bank.question: Which three of the following are significant long-term health risks that a supervisor must manage on a construction site?

Hand-arm vibration syndrome (HAVS)
Silicosis from breathing in crystalline silica dust
Asbestos-related lung diseases

Personally supervising every individual worker for the duration of the shift

bank.question: What is the primary piece of legislation that governs health and safety in the UK?

The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974

The Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015

bank.question: It is the supervisor's responsibility to ensure that exclusion zones are maintained around active plant or machinery

bank.question: Which three of these are environmental responsibilities for a site supervisor?

Managing noise and dust to prevent complaints from local residents
Increasing the amount of waste sent to landfill to clear the site faster

bank.question: A near miss should be ignored if nobody was actually injured

bank.question: COSHH applies to hazardous substances such as certain dusts, fumes, solvents and cement products

bank.question: Which two actions are most effective at reducing the risk of Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS)?

Encouraging workers to grip the tool as tightly as possible

A minor cut that only requires a plaster from the first-aid kit
A persistent headache caused by a loud site environment
Occupational asthma caused by exposure to sensitising chemicals

bank.question: Harnesses should normally be used without a rescue plan

bank.question: In accordance with fire safety management, how often must fire extinguishers on a construction site be professionally serviced?

Once every 6 months

Only when the gauge indicates low pressure

The project's environmental waste plan
A standard fire risk assessment

bank.question: Working on or near live electrical systems should only be permitted if it is unreasonable for the power to be turned off

bank.question: Under CDM 2015, who is primarily responsible for managing health and safety risks during the design and planning phase?

Principal Designer

Clear reversing arrangements and trained banksmen where needed
Allowing pedestrians to use vehicle routes as shortcuts
Good visibility, signage and exclusion zones

bank.question: Which of the following incidents must be reported to the HSE under RIDDOR?

A brief dizzy spell
A fractured arm
A lost site ID card

bank.question: What is the main purpose of a site induction for a new worker?

To explain site-specific hazards, emergency procedures, and welfare locations

To negotiate the worker's pay and hours for the project

bank.question: Silica dust can damage the lungs even where the dust cloud appears small

12V (battery power)

In the worker's pocket for easy access throughout the day

bank.question: What is a supervisor's main role in managing occupational health on site?

Monitoring day-to-day worker health and spotting early signs of ill-health

At the start of every shift before work begins

bank.question: Which regulations define the roles of the Principal Designer and Principal Contractor?

bank.question: An Improvement Notice gives time to correct a breach of health and safety law

bank.question: Regarding Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), what is a supervisor's main responsibility?

Does the worker have a valid harness and lanyard?
How many people are required to hold the access equipment?

bank.question: Under the Work at Height Regulations, collective protection measures must be prioritised over personal protection measures
bank.explanation: This is true because the Hierarchy of Control prioritizes collective measures (like scaffolding) that protect everyone over individual measures (like harnesses) that only protect the wearer

bank.question: What should a supervisor do if they see a worker from a different subcontractor ignoring safety rules?
bank.explanation: Supervisors should lead by example; ignoring breaches undermines safety culture and suggests that rules are optional
options: Wait until the next scheduled safety meeting to mention it
Stop the work immediately and address the breach with the worker
Contact the worker's employer after they have finished for the day
Note it in the site diary but take no further action if no one was hurt

bank.question: Before allowing a team to enter a confined space, which three steps must a supervisor take?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A, B and C. The supervisor must check the permit is valid, the area is tested for gas, and the person entering the space is medically fit
options: Ensuring a valid Confined Space Entry Permit is in place and signed
Confirming that gas monitoring equipment has been calibrated and used
Checking that the entrant is trained and has the correct rescue equipment
Checking that the entrant has their personal mobile phone for emergencies

bank.question: According to the hierarchy of risk control, what is the most effective way to manage a hazard?
bank.explanation: In the hierarchy of control, elimination is always the most effective measure, followed by substitution and engineering controls
options: Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
Eliminating the hazard entirely
Administrative controls and training
Engineering controls like guarding

bank.question: What is the most significant health hazard associated with 'dry cutting' concrete blocks with a power saw?
bank.explanation: Silica dust (RCS) is highly toxic and can cause silicosis and lung cancer; it is commonly produced when cutting concrete, bricks, or stone
options: Silica dust (RCS)
Wood shavings
General household dust
Water vapour from a pressure washer

bank.question: What is the most effective way to control dust when using a cut-off saw on concrete?
bank.explanation: Dust suppression (water) or local exhaust ventilation (LEV) are the primary methods for reducing respiratory risks at the source
options: Use power tools fitted with dust extraction or water suppression
Ensure the worker is wearing a standard cloth comfort mask
Tell the worker to stand upwind of the dust cloud
Wait for a rainy day to perform the cutting work outdoors

bank.question: When a task requires the use of a ladder, which two safety checks must a supervisor perform?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. Supervisors must check that ladders are for low-risk, short-duration work and are in good condition through pre-use inspections
options: Confirming the work is short duration (less than 30 minutes) and low risk
Ensuring the ladder is made of metal if working near live electricity
Checking that the ladder has been inspected and displays a valid tag
Mandating that workers carry heavy loads in one hand while climbing

bank.question: What is the main reason for a 'Permit to Work' system on a construction site?
bank.explanation: A Permit to Work provides a formal safety check and controlled procedure for high-risk activities like working in confined spaces
options: To ensure the worker gets paid a higher rate for the task
To prove that the company has employer's liability insurance
To provide a formal safety check for high-risk activities
To bypass the need for a standard risk assessment

bank.question: Fire exits should be kept clear even during short deliveries
bank.explanation: This is true because blocked escape routes can delay evacuation during an emergency.

bank.question: When reviewing Risk Assessments and Method Statements (RAMS), which two statements are true?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. RAMS must be specific to the tasks performed and must be read, understood, and signed by those doing the work
options: They must be specific to the task and site location
They are only required for work lasting more than 30 days
They must be signed by the operatives before work starts
They serve as a legal substitute for the Health and Safety at Work Act

bank.question: When supervising work in a confined space, which three safety measures are mandatory?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A, C and D. Confined spaces (like manholes or tanks) require trained staff, a permit to work, and gas monitoring to detect lethal atmospheres. High-visibility vests do not provide protection
options: Workers must be specifically trained and competent in confined space entry
A 'Permit to Work' must be issued and signed before entry
Atmospheric testing (gas monitoring) must be conducted before and during entry
Only one person is allowed in the space at a time to save oxygen

bank.question: New electrical power tools do not require a formal inspection or PAT test until they have been used for at least six months
bank.explanation: This is false because all portable electrical equipment should be tested (PAT) and inspected at regular intervals, regardless of whether it is new

bank.question: How should a supervisor manage a worker who does not speak or understand English well?
bank.explanation: Supervisors have a legal and moral duty to ensure all workers, regardless of their native language, fully understand the safety instructions and risks
options: Provide information through translated documents, pictures, or a competent translator
Ask the worker to use an online translation app on their phone while working
Tell the worker to follow another experienced person and copy what they do
Assume the worker has enough basic knowledge from previous sites to work safely

bank.question: In which of these scenarios would a supervisor definitely require a 'Permit to Work' to be issued?
bank.explanation: A Permit to Work is required for high-risk activities where standard safe systems of work are not sufficient to manage the specific hazards
options: Whenever a worker is working overtime
For all general site activities throughout the day
For high-risk activities such as work in confined spaces or on live HV systems
Only when a scaffolding platform is over 5 metres high

bank.question: Which site risk is specifically covered by the COSHH Regulations?
bank.explanation: COSHH assessments are required for any substance that could be hazardous to health, including wood dust, silica dust, and chemical fumes
options: Electricity and trailing cables
Manual handling of heavy bricks
Working near moving plant and machinery
Exposure to hazardous substances like silica dust

bank.question: A worker is injured on site. What should be the supervisor's immediate priority?
bank.explanation: A supervisor's first step after an accident is to secure the area to prevent further harm and then ensure help is provided
options: Make the area safe and ensure first aid is administered
Call the HSE immediately before doing anything else
Gather everyone for a toolbox talk to discuss the event
Remove any evidence that might lead to a fine

bank.question: A method statement should describe the safe sequence of work for a specific task
bank.explanation: This is true because method statements explain how the task will be carried out safely, including controls, responsibilities and sequencing.

bank.question: What is the primary cause of Weil's Disease (Leptospirosis) on a construction site?
bank.explanation: Leptospirosis is commonly spread through the urine of rats and is a significant risk for those working near water or sewers
options: Contact with asbestos fibres
Contact with water or soil contaminated by rat urine
Inhaling silica dust from concrete cutting
Long-term exposure to loud machinery noise

bank.question: A rescue plan for work at height should be practical and understood before work starts
bank.explanation: This is true because a delayed or improvised rescue can lead to further harm after a fall.

bank.question: Excavations can collapse even when the ground appears firm
bank.explanation: This is true because soil stability can change and excavations need support, battering or other suitable controls.

bank.question: If a site needs to pump out water from an excavation (dewatering), where is it generally unacceptable to discharge it without treatment?
bank.explanation: An 'Environment Agency' or local authority permit is usually required for discharging any water that isn't clean rainwater into the sewer
options: Into the nearest surface water drain
Directly into a nearby watercourse or stream
Onto the open ground to let it soak away
Into the foul sewer only with prior permission/agreement

bank.question: Which three of the following are hazardous substances that a supervisor should monitor for on a refurbishment site?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A, B and D. Asbestos, CO, and Lead are hazardous substances requiring controls. Noise is a physical hazard, and Wood dust is a substance, but the question asks for 'substances' (often chemical/biological/gas). Correct answers focus on COSHH-relevant toxic substances
options: Asbestos fibres released during demolition
Carbon Monoxide (CO) from petrol-driven pumps in enclosed spaces
Noise levels from heavy piling machinery
Lead dust or fumes during refurbishment of old structures

bank.question: Under RIDDOR, only fatal accidents need to be reported to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE)
bank.explanation: This is false because a site supervisor must report 'Specified Injuries' and 'Dangerous Occurrences' to the HSE under RIDDOR regulations

bank.question: All lifting equipment must be clearly marked with its Safe Working Load (SWL)
bank.explanation: This is true because supervisors must ensure that all lifting equipment has a current Report of Thorough Examination as required by LOLER

bank.question: Which two examples are most likely to require a permit-to-work system?
bank.explanation: The correct answers are A and B. Permits help control higher-risk activities such as confined space entry and hot works.
options: Entry into a confined space
Hot works near combustible materials
Routine office printing
Making tea in the welfare unit

bank.question: According to the Hierarchy of Control for working at height, what is the first priority?
bank.explanation: Work at height regulation requires that the first consideration must always be to avoid working at height if the task can be done from the ground
options: Avoid working at height altogether
Use a harness and lanyard
Install safety netting below the work area
Ensure a supervisor is watching at all times

bank.question: Which document outlines the health and safety arrangements for the entire duration of a construction project?
bank.explanation: Supervisors are often responsible for ensuring the Construction Phase Plan, developed by the Principal Contractor, is followed on the ground level
options: The Health and Safety File
The Construction Phase Plan (CPP)
The Pre-construction information document
The Planning Application forms

bank.question: What is a supervisor's responsibility regarding fire safety on site?
bank.explanation: A supervisor must ensure the workplace is safe for their team; this includes checking that fire exits are clear and accessible
options: Ensure fire exit routes are kept clear and doors are functional
Install and wire the site-wide fire alarm system
Call the local fire brigade to request a site inspection
Personally test every fire extinguisher once a week

bank.question: After a Risk Assessment and Method Statement (RAMS) has been produced, what is the supervisor's main responsibility?
bank.explanation: Supervisors must ensure workers are aware of risks and the specific measures required to mitigate them before work starts
options: Communicate the findings and controls to the work team
File the document away in the site office immediately
Only show it to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) if asked
Keep it secret to avoid worrying the workforce

bank.question: Which safety sign shape and colour indicate a 'mandatory' requirement, such as 'Hard Hats Must Be Worn'?
bank.explanation: Signs with a blue circle and a white symbol indicate that a specific action or PPE 'must' be taken or worn
options: A yellow triangle with a black border
A blue circle with a white symbol
A red circle with a diagonal line
A green square with a white symbol

bank.question: What is the purpose of a Workplace Exposure Limit (WEL)?
bank.explanation: Work exposure limits (WELs) are set to protect workers from the long-term effects of inhaling hazardous substances like silica dust
options: To determine the weight of the material being handled on site
To set the maximum concentration of an airborne substance averaged over a period of time
To calculate the total number of hours a person can work outdoors
To measure the noise levels produced by heavy plant machinery
